title: Tiered KV cache quantization playbook and FP8→INT4 fidelity probe
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Produce an actionable playbook and empirical dataset for a tiered KV cache strategy that adaptively selects compression formats (FP8, INT8, INT4) by request cohort and recency, minimizing GPU memory while bounding generation quality regressions. Background: we currently apply uniform KV cache formats which leaves capacity on the table for high-concurrency workloads. Hypothesis: a small fraction of recent KV entries require higher fidelity (FP32/FP16/FP8) while older or less-accessed entries can be aggressively quantized to INT8/INT4 without impacting downstream token quality for most user cohorts. Experiment design: 1) Implement a prototype tiered cache in the runtime that tags KV entries with an age-and-frequency score and places them into one of three physical tiers: high-fidelity (FP8), medium (INT8), low (INT4). 2) Build a deterministic fallback path for dynamic dequantization to higher fidelity for cases where the model indicates high sensitivity (attention weight spikes, logit change heuristics). 3) Run controlled A/B microbenchmarks across representative workloads (assistant chat, long-context summarization, code completion) with a fixed batching policy to isolate KV effects. 4) Measure end-to-end metrics: per-token latency, tail latency (p95/p99), throughput, peak GPU memory, token-level perplexity/LL delta on held-out prompts, application-level quality (ROUGE/BLEU and human-evaluated pass/fail checks), and cost-per-token. Safety nets & acceptance criteria: maximum allowed delta in model log-likelihood: -0.5 to +0.1 bits/token for P95 of prompts; human-eval degradation <= 3% for high-value cohorts; peak GPU memory reduction >= 18% for INT4-inclusive tiering compared to baseline. Rollout plan: staged canary on runtime-2.4: dev cluster -> internal dogfood -> 10% external traffic -> ramp with automated regression gate. Rollback: instant fallback to uniform FP8 cache format and disable tiering if quality regressions exceed thresholds or GPU OOM incidents occur. Deliverables: playbook doc with parameter tuning guidance, an evaluation dataset and aggregated benchmark results, a runtime flag set and perf microbench PR, and a dashboard to monitor per-cohort quality and memory gains.
steps: Implement tiered cache allocator that maps age+freq score to tier
Add lightweight on-request sensitivity detector to trigger on-demand dequantization
Instrument KV read/write paths with counters and size metrics
Create evaluation harness that replays production traces with deterministic batching
Run full sweep across FP8/INT8/INT4 mixes and collect quality/cost metrics
Merge runtime changes behind feature flag and start canary
tests: Unit: correctness of quantize/dequantize round-trips across formats
Perf: simulated 2k concurrent connections replay with target batch sizes
Quality: LL delta and human-eval checks against benchmark prompts
Stability: OOM injection tests and graceful degradation verification
